bugs.what: The 'Aldric's Ring' quest completed via a ledger check at the Company Store (Cinderhall), but I still carried the physical 'Aldric's iron ring' item for the rest of the game with no dialogue option to actually hand it to Corporal Fenn — talking to him only offered a debt-info line, not an item-delivery line, leaving the item's purpose unresolved.
bugs.where: The Company Store (Cinderhall) / Corporal Fenn at Highward's Barracks

bugs.what: Claiming the Regent's Writ at Highward retroactively spawned an urgent-sounding 'Ironbound column burning the Reach' consequence quest with no prior warning or way to weigh that cost before accepting the writ.
bugs.where: The Captain-General's Hall, Marrowgate envoy dialogue

bugs.what: Random small-room mazes (e.g. Thornwold's Split Beech/Deer Break/Black Thorn Stand cluster, Wardmoor's Peat Score/Tower Rise cluster) had many directionally identical-looking exits, causing repeated backtracking loops even with the free 'get bearings' action, since bearings often didn't list the specific landmark being sought until much closer to it.

confusions: Long 'travel to a known place' lists paginate in fixed chunks of ~10 with a 'X more' entry that sometimes required multiple clicks to reach the desired destination, with no search/filter.

It wasn't always clear whether 'weigh what this grief asks' had already surfaced every resolution path for a hollow, or whether new paths would unlock later (e.g. the oath-stone at Wardmoor only revealed the 'speak the Great Rite' option after becoming a sworn Keeper elsewhere, not before).
suggestions: Let inventory quest-items that no longer have a valid delivery target auto-resolve or clearly say 'nothing more to do with this' instead of persisting silently.
Surface the consequence of accepting a faction-costing reward (like the Regent's Writ) before confirming it, not after.
Add a lightweight compass/quest-arrow in the free 'look'/'bearings' output that always points toward the nearest unresolved quest marker, even from a distance.

For companion regard-conflicts resolved via a will check, consider lowering the DC or removing the double-disapproval penalty on a failed 'settle it' attempt, since it currently punishes the diplomatic option harder than just picking a side.
